answer: Paired-Use Coordination Levy.** Each identity must hold a distinct marble token and a distinct lantern token, matched in a public pairing ledger; transactions between two identities consume one pair from each side. A juniper signature tags every match, so reuse of either token across identities is detectable and voids the pair. An attacker running N sybils must acquire and irreversibly consume N distinct pairs per coordination round, paying full acquisition cost plus forfeiture on detection, so marginal cost of each additional identity scales with pairing scarcity rather than a flat fee.
